The State Arrival Ceremony featured the United States Armed Forces, including a military review, performances by the United States Army Old Guard Fife and Drum Corps, the United States Marine Corps Silent Drill Platoon, and “The Commandant’s Own” United States Marine Drum and Bugle Corps, and concluded with a military flyover featuring a B-2 Spirit and four F-22 Raptors.

Following the Ceremony, the First Lady hosted Madame Peng for a special cultural program at the Smithsonian’s National Museum of Asian Art, where they explored works representing centuries of artistic achievement and cultural exchange.

Their visit included a viewing of a notched jade disk dating to China’s Shang dynasty, followed by the Smithsonian’s celebrated Peacock Room, created by American artist James McNeill Whistler. The First Lady and Madame Peng also viewed an 18th-century Qianlong-period Chinese porcelain vase, showcasing the extraordinary craftsmanship and decorative sophistication of imperial Chinese porcelain.

The program concluded with the youth choir from Hope Chinese School performing “Jasmine Flower” and “Songs & Smiles” for the First Lady and Madame Peng. The children’s voices offered a fitting close to the visit, celebrating the beauty of artistic expression and the promise of the next generation.

The First Lady led preparations for the State Dinner in the East Room of the White House later that evening, bringing together American culinary traditions and subtle Chinese influences.

On Friday morning, the President and First Lady welcomed President Xi and Madame Peng to the White House for tea in the Red Room, continuing the traditions of hospitality that have long accompanied visits by foreign leaders and their spouses.

Following tea, the President and First Lady accompanied President Xi and Madame Peng to the National Archives, where they viewed important records and documents highlighting America’s 250th birthday as well as important chapters in the history of the relationship between the United States and China. The visit offered an opportunity to reflect upon the history shared between two nations while looking toward the future.

The State Visit concluded at the National Archives, where the President and First Lady bid farewell to President Xi and Madame Peng.

First Lady Melania Trump and Madame Peng Liyuan visited the Smithsonian National Museum of Asian Art in Washington, DC today, where they explored works spanning centuries of artistic achievement and cultural exchange and shared a special moment with students from the Washington, DC area.

Upon arrival, the First Lady and Madame Peng were welcomed by leadership of the Smithsonian National Museum of Asian Art before beginning their tour of the museum’s collections.

The First Lady and Madame Peng then viewed the Smithsonian’s celebrated Peacock Room, one of the museum’s most distinctive and immersive works of art.

Created by American artist James McNeill Whistler in 1876–77, the Peacock Room transforms an entire interior into a dazzling composition of blue, green, and gold. Inspired in significant part by Chinese porcelain and Japanese design, Whistler covered the room with shimmering patterns and fanciful depictions of peacocks, creating a singular work in which painting, architecture, and decorative arts converge. Purchased by American collector Charles Lang Freer in 1904, the room was transported from London to the United States and has been a centerpiece of the museum in Washington since 1923.

Today, the Peacock Room stands as a remarkable meeting point of American art and Asian artistic traditions, reflecting the ways artists and collectors have found inspiration across cultures and generations.

The First Lady and Madame Peng continued their visit with a viewing of a Qianlong-period Chinese porcelain vase, dating to the 18th century. Produced in Jingdezhen during the Qing dynasty, the vase features elaborate floral decoration executed in colorful famille rose enamels, gold, and iron red over a pale glaze. The work is part of the Freer Gallery of Art’s collection and reflects the extraordinary technical and decorative sophistication of imperial Chinese porcelain during the Qianlong era.

Museum leadership who served as guides for the visit were Jan Stuart, Melvin R. Seiden Curator of Chinese Art at the National Museum of Asian Art, and Chase Robinson, Dame Jillian Sackler Director of the Arthur M. Sackler Gallery and Freer Gallery of Art.

The visit concluded with a musical performance by the youth choir from Hope Chinese School, who performed “Jasmine Flower” and “Songs & Smiles” for the First Lady and Madame Peng. The young students’ performance offered a joyful and memorable conclusion to the visit, bringing together the beauty of artistic expression, the appreciation of cultural heritage, and the shared experience of young people discovering the enduring power of art and music.

Melania and I join all those celebrating the life and legacy of Archbishop Fulton J. Sheen—the Catholic priest who pioneered the use of media to speak the truth, preach the Gospel, and bring many souls closer to Christ.  Today, Archbishop Sheen will become the first-ever American-born bishop to be beatified by the Catholic Church.

Born on the plains of central Illinois at the twilight of the nineteenth century, Fulton Sheen was blessed with extraordinary intelligence, good humor, and eloquence.  After his ordination to the priesthood, he spent more than two decades teaching, lecturing, and broadcasting on the radio before he was consecrated Auxiliary Bishop of New York in 1951.  With a growing reputation as a world-class preacher and evangelist, he then launched his renowned national television series, Life Is Worth Living, which soon captivated the entire country.

On his show, Archbishop Sheen lectured before a live audience on an array of theological, philosophical, and political topics.  Dressed in striking priestly robes and armed with only a chalk stick and blackboard, he quickly emerged as a primetime sensation—boldly bringing the teachings of Christianity to a world threatened by the titanic forces of communism.

Archbishop Sheen shocked the entertainment industry by besting American legends like Milton Berle and Frank Sinatra in weekly ratings, winning an Emmy award for Most Outstanding Television Personality, and appearing on the cover of Time magazine.  For years, his sharp wit and piercing intellect filled millions of American living rooms and converted thousands—including national politicians, Hollywood celebrities, and communist leaders—to the Catholic faith.  His program attracted an estimated 30 million weekly viewers, ultimately becoming one of the most watched religious programs in the history of television.  Through it all, Archbishop Sheen used his platform not for his own sake but to strengthen our Nation with the good news of the Gospel.

In the 1960s, against the rising tide of anti-God extremism in American culture, Archbishop Sheen turned to the camera to identify a “new type of violence that’s sweeping our country, our schools, and our streets.”  This violence, he warned in his later career The Fulton Sheen Program, “involves destruction of everything that is in the past.”  He continued, “Our Nation is too full of those that are crying, “Down… Down with schools.  Down with the churches.  Down with teachers.  Down with government.  Down with the police.  Can you build anything down?” he implored the Nation.  “You cannot… Let’s begin now to use the word ‘Up.’  Up from all of this filth.  Up from this violence… Up—up to God.”

Sheen was later appointed as the Bishop of Rochester, New York, and the titular Archbishop of Newport, Wales.  In October 1979, Pope John Paul II, the leader of the Roman Catholic Church, embraced Archbishop Sheen in Saint Patrick’s Cathedral in New York City, telling him, “You have written and spoken well of the Lord Jesus.  You are a loyal son of the Church.”  Archbishop Sheen died just two months later while praying in his private chapel.

Archbishop Fulton Sheen’s legacy endures in homes, churches, and communities all across our country.  Countless Americans still watch recordings of his broadcasts and read his books.  The Archbishop Fulton J. Sheen Museum in his native Illinois attracts thousands of visitors every year.  And today, as thousands of Americans gather in St. Louis, Missouri, for his Beatification Mass, we pray that Archbishop Sheen’s heroic commitment to nourishing the soul of our country will inspire others to follow his example and lift our Nation upward and ever higher to God.

President Donald J. Trump and First Lady Melania Trump will welcome His Excellency Xi Jinping, President of The People’s Republic of China, and Madame Peng Liyuan for a State Dinner in the East Room of the White House this evening. The First Lady led the preparations for the dinner, which will be attended by the official delegations as well as business leaders and government officials.

MENU

The menu showcases American ingredients with subtle Chinese influence, bringing the culinary traditions of both nations together. The meal begins with a toast of Schramsberg “Blanc De Noir,” honoring the historic “Toast to Peace” shared by President Nixon and Premier Zhou Enlai in Beijing in 1972. The same American sparkling wine served at that historic gathering continues to be enjoyed at White House functions today.

First Course
Yellow Squash Velouté
Wild Mushroom FricasséeCrispy Pancetta
Scallion Oil

The first course offers a refined and silky-smooth velouté made of sweet yellow squash. This course is gently blended to highlight its delicate seasonal flavors of earthy wild mushrooms, sautéed with fresh herbs. Together, these ingredients create a rich fricassee, complemented by crispy pancetta for a savory and smoky contrast. A finishing drizzle of scallion oil adds vibrance and a subtle allium brightness to the dish.

Second Course
Sesame Crusted Sea Bass
Braised Baby Bok ChoyRoasted Garden Eggplant
Sauce Verte

The second course is prepared delicately with fresh seabass and coated in toasted sesame seeds. This combination creates a fragrant nutty crust while keeping the fish tender. The fish is served with crisp baby bok choy and roasted garden eggplant, creating lightly caramelized flavors. The dish is finished with a vibrant sauce verte of fresh herbs, which add brightness, acidity, and a garden character.

Dessert
Vanilla Crémeux & White House Honey Ice Cream
Walnut FrangipaneSour Cherry Confit The dessert course is a smooth vanilla crémeux with a vibrant sour cherry confit center, set a top a rich walnut frangipane. The dessert’s fruit shaped form is complimented by a delicate ice cream made with harvested White House honey.

ENTERTAINMENT

There will be several performances during the formal dinner, which will be headlined by Mr. Christopher Macchio, a classically trained tenor who performed at the 2025 Presidential Inauguration. The evening’s entertainment will feature performances by military musicians from the United States Marines Corps and the United States Army, including “The President’s Own” United States Marine Band, “The Commandant’s Own” United States Marine Drum and Bugle Corps, the United States Army Chorus, and the United States Army Strings.

FLORAL & DÉCOR

The décor for the evening is an expression of warmth and celebration and draws on the color red’s longstanding cultural significance throughout Chinese history. Urns showcase overflowing red blossoms. Tables are dressed in rich red linens and adorned with dahlias and ranunculus. Among the seasonal blooms, the tables feature vermeil from the White House collection. The Reagan State Service is featured on the tables. These details blend Chinese artistry and American tradition together, showcased within the timeless elegance of the White House.

Today, President Donald J. Trump joined leaders of Denmark and Greenland to sign an unprecedented agreement giving the United States lasting control over security interests in Greenland. The landmark agreement — which comes at no cost to American taxpayers — forever guarantees America the ability to defend the continent, includes permanent basing rights, and bars any U.S. adversary from establishing a base, military presence, or sensitive investment without America’s approval.

The agreement is being hailed at home and around the world as a decisive victory for American security and a stronger NATO in the Arctic. Here’s what they’re saying:

President Donald J. Trump: “As I announced just days ago, the U.S. has also reached an unprecedented agreement regarding the Northern Frontier of North America — the large and strategically vital piece of land known as Greenland. This agreement… gives the United States permanent control over security and all other needs on that territory. We will have the complete ability to do what is necessary to defend the American continent.”

Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen: “This day represents a milestone in our longstanding cooperation. 75 years ago, we entered into an agreement about the defense of Greenland. Today, we are signing an even bigger and better agreement — a deal that can last forever. This deal is good for the United States, it’s good for Greenland, for Denmark, for the NATO alliance, and therefore, also good for Europe. In other words, we are strengthening our common security, boosting our common deterrence, showing our adversaries who we are — and we are doing it together.”

Prime Minister of Greenland Jens-Frederik Nielsen: “We are, have been, and will remain a steadfast friend of the United States and a part of the Western alliance. Your security is our security and our security is your security. We are truly pleased with the result that strengthens our shared security and strengthens our bond as close allies. This agreement is historical.”

Danish Minister for Foreign Affairs Lars Løkke Rasmussen: “An important moment today. Greenland, Denmark and the United States have signed an agreement strengthening security in the Arctic and North Atlantic. It’s been a bumpy ride. But here we are – with a deal in hand that we can all be very satisfied with. We share a long history. And we share a responsibility for the security of our region. Today, we take another important step together – with full respect for the sovereignty and territorial integrity of the Kingdom of Denmark and the Greenlandic people’s right to self-determination. History binds us together. Our future demands that we stand together.”

NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte: “Great to see the deal signed by the United States, Denmark, and Greenland today. We know the threats we face, and greater security in the Arctic and North Atlantic is essential for Europe and North America alike. This agreement, along with NATO’s growing role in securing this vital region, enhances our collective security and supports a safer and more stable future for us all”

European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen: “I welcome today’s agreement on strengthening security in the Arctic and North Atlantic. My visit to Greenland earlier this month underscored the strategic importance of the region and the scale of the challenges. Challenges we will face together. As always, the EU will work closely with Denmark and Greenland and our international partners.”

German Chancellor Friedrich Merz: “Good news for the security of Greenland: The agreement between Denmark, Greenland, and the USA strengthens our partnership in NATO and security in the High North. Our partners can count on the support of Germany.”

Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre: “I welcome the agreement between Greenland, Denmark and the USA. It is a good diplomatic solution, important for stability and security in the [Arctic].”

Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni: “Well done on the agreement between the United States, Denmark, and Greenland. The Arctic is a strategic area: security is built together.”

Estonian Minister of Foreign Affairs Margus Tsahkna: “Estonia welcomes the agreement reached by Denmark, Greenland and the United States to strengthen security in the Arctic. Enhanced cooperation among NATO Allies in Greenland and the Arctic reinforces the security of the Alliance and of Europe as a whole. Close and coordinated cooperation among Allies remains the most effective way to strengthen deterrence and defence in the region.”

Swedish Minister for Foreign Affairs Maria Malmer Stenergard: “I welcome that Denmark, Greenland and the United States have reached an agreement on strengthened security in the Arctic and North-Atlantic area. Sweden remains committed to working with all our Allies to improve our common security.”

Secretary of State Marco Rubio: “This historic deal is a huge win for the United States and the American people. Thanks to President Trump’s vision and leadership, this historic agreement permanently guarantees U.S. security interests in the Arctic at zero cost to the U.S. taxpayer. Greenland will forever be part of the strategic defense area of North America and exclude any adversary from it and the surrounding area. This deal permanently and completely addresses our national security concerns in Greenland.”

U.S. Ambassador to the United Nations Mike Waltz: “History in the making at UNGA as President Trump seals his landmark deal with Denmark and Greenland ensuring American national security and defense in the Arctic region.”

U.S. Ambassador to Denmark Kenneth Howery: “Historic day for the United States, Denmark, and Greenland. A tremendous honor to join President Trump, Prime Minister Frederiksen, and Prime Minister Nielsen in New York today as they sign an agreement to ensure all three of our countries’ security for generations to come.”

U.S. Special Envoy to Greenland Jeff Landry: “This is a great day for America and for our national security interests. Well done President @realDonaldTrump and @SecRubio! With the signing of this deal, American interests in the Arctic have never been more secure. This is America First. This is promises made, promises kept!”

Former Speaker of the House Newt Gingrich: “In 1946, President Truman’s administration explored purchasing Greenland because of its importance to American defense. Eighty years later, President Trump has announced a new Arctic security agreement. The geography hasn’t changed. The strategic competition has.”

Former Deputy National Security Advisor KT McFarland: “Game changer”

Former National Security Council Chief of Staff Alex Gray: “Nearly two years ago I wrote in @WSJopinion that POTUS should actually buy #Greenland. He has now scored a remarkable victory that accomplishes those goals without the cost.”

Center for Security Policy Senior Fellow Col. Grant Newsham (ret.): “This is a big deal. This is right up there with Secretary of State Seward getting Alaska. It’s a little different because we haven’t bought the place, but it locks up or brings into the fold, really, key terrain, key geography, up on our northeast… Russia and the Chinese, in particular, they can’t get in there militarily, and they cannot get in economically.”

Washington Times Editorial Board: “Coming on the heels of his Venezuela triumph — access to the world’s largest known oil reserves — President Trump’s Greenland deal caps his status as one of history’s great dealmakers.”

Commentator Scott Jennings: “Donald Trump was right about Greenland from the beginning… and finally, we got it done. This historic agreement between the United States and Denmark gives Donald Trump everything we wanted and everything we needed as it relates to the future security of Greenland.”

Claremont Institute Senior Fellow Jeremy Carl: “This is a major win for which President Trump, Secretary Rubio and the administration are not getting nearly enough credit.
